  "extractions": [

      "unit": "F001:F004",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "definition",
        "scope_quotes": [
          "F001"
        ],
        "scope_text": "For employees of a covered employer under 29 CFR 825.110(a).",
        "context_quotes": [
          "F003",
          "F004"
        ],
        "modality_quote": "",
        "modality": "not_stated",
        "alternative_quotes": [
          "F002",
          "F003",
          "F004"
        ],
        "choice_quote": "F001:F004",
        "choice_text": "An eligible employee must satisfy all three criteria: (1) has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, and (2) has been employed for at least 1,250 hours of service during the 12-month period immediately preceding the commencement of the leave, and (3) is employed at a worksite where 50 or more employees are employed by the employer within 75 miles of that worksite.",
        "logic_quote": "F001:F004",
        "references": [
          "§ 825.801",
          "§ 825.105(b)"
        ],
        "statement": "An eligible employee is defined as an employee of a covered employer who has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, has been employed for at least 1,250 hours of service during the 12-month period immediately preceding the commencement of the leave, and is employed at a worksite where 50 or more employees are employed by the employer within 75 miles of that worksite."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F005",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "exemption",
        "scope_quotes": [
          "F005"
        ],
        "scope_text": "In determining the 12 months an employee must have been employed by the employer under 29 CFR 825.110(b).",
        "context_quotes": [
          "F006"
        ],
        "modality_quote": "need not be",
        "modality": "not_required",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F005",
        "references": [],
        "statement": "The 12 months an employee must have been employed by the employer need not be consecutive months, provided the rules governing breaks in service are met."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F006",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "exemption",
        "scope_quotes": [
          "F006"
        ],
        "scope_text": "In determining whether an employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, subject to the exceptions provided in paragraph (b)(2).",
        "context_quotes": [
          "F007:F009"
        ],
        "modality_quote": "need not be",
        "modality": "not_required",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F006",
        "references": [
          "paragraph (b)(2)"
        ],
        "statement": "Subject to the exceptions provided in paragraph (b)(2) of this section, employment periods prior to a break in service of seven years or more need not be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F007:F009",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "requirement",
        "scope_quotes": [
          "F007"
        ],
        "scope_text": "In determining whether an employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months where there is a break in service of more than seven years under paragraph (b)(2).",
        "context_quotes": [
          "F008"
        ],
        "modality_quote": "must be",
        "modality": "must",
        "alternative_quotes": [
          "F008",
          "F009"
        ],
        "choice_quote": "F007:F009",
        "choice_text": "Employment periods preceding a break in service of more than seven years must be counted where either: (i) the break in service is occasioned by fulfillment of USERRA-covered service obligation, or (ii) a written agreement, including a collective bargaining agreement, exists concerning the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break in service.",
        "logic_quote": "F007:F009",
        "references": [
          "38 U.S.C. 4301, et seq."
        ],
        "statement": "Employment periods preceding a break in service of more than seven years must be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months where the employee's break in service is occasioned by fulfillment of a USERRA-covered service obligation (and the period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service must also be counted, without providing any greater entitlement than available under USERRA), or where a written agreement, including a collective bargaining agreement, exists concerning the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break in service."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F010",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "statement",
        "scope_quotes": [
          "F010"
        ],
        "scope_text": "When an employee is maintained on the payroll for any part of a week, or when determining whether intermittent/occasional/casual employment qualifies as at least 12 months.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "",
        "modality": "not_stated",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F010",
        "references": [],
        "statement": "If an employee is maintained on the payroll for any part of a week, including any periods of paid or unpaid leave (sick, vacation) during which other benefits or compensation are provided by the employer (such as workers' compensation or group health plan benefits), the week counts as a week of employment; for intermittent, occasional, or casual employment, 52 weeks is deemed equal to 12 months."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F011",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "requirement",
        "scope_quotes": [
          "F011"
        ],
        "scope_text": "When an employer chooses to recognize prior employment before a continuous break in service of more than seven years in determining whether an employee met the 12-month requirement.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "must",
        "modality": "must",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F011",
        "references": [],
        "statement": "Nothing prevents employers from considering employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years when determining whether an employee has met the 12-month employment requirement, but if an employer chooses to recognize such prior employment, the employer must do so uniformly with respect to all employees with similar breaks in service."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F012",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "permission",
        "scope_quotes": [
          "F012"
        ],
        "scope_text": "In determining whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service, except as provided in paragraph (c)(2) and § 825.801 for airline flight crew employees.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "may be",
        "modality": "may",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F012",
        "references": [
          "paragraph (c)(2)",
          "§ 825.801",
          "29 CFR part 785"
        ],
        "statement": "Except as provided in paragraph (c)(2) and § 825.801, whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service is determined according to FLSA principles for compensable hours of work based on actual hours worked for the employer, unconstrained by recordkeeping methods or inaccurate compensation agreements, and any accurate accounting of actual hours worked under FLSA principles may be used."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F013",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "requirement",
        "scope_quotes": [
          "F013"
        ],
        "scope_text": "When determining FMLA eligibility for an employee returning from USERRA-covered service.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "shall be",
        "modality": "must",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F013",
        "references": [
          "§ 825.801(c)"
        ],
        "statement": "An employee returning from USERRA-covered service shall be credited with the hours of service that would have been performed but for the period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service (added to hours actually worked during the previous 12-month period to meet the hours of service requirement), and the employee's pre-service work schedule can generally be used for calculations."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F014",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "requirement",
        "scope_quotes": [
          "F014"
        ],
        "scope_text": "In the event an employer does not maintain an accurate record of hours worked by an employee, including FLSA recordkeeping-exempt employees.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "must be",
        "modality": "must",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F014",
        "references": [
          "29 CFR part 541",
          "§ 825.102",
          "§ 825.801(d)"
        ],
        "statement": "In the event an employer does not maintain an accurate record of hours worked by an employee (including FLSA-exempt employees), the employer has the burden of showing that the employee has not worked the requisite hours, and must be able to clearly demonstrate that the employee did not work 1,250 hours during the previous 12 months in order to claim that the employee is not eligible for FMLA leave."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F015",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "requirement",
        "scope_quotes": [
          "F015"
        ],
        "scope_text": "Under 29 CFR 825.110(d) regarding the timing of eligibility determinations.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "must be",
        "modality": "must",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F015",
        "references": [
          "§ 825.300(b)"
        ],
        "statement": "The determination of whether an employee meets the hours of service requirement and has been employed by the employer for a total of at least 12 months must be made as of the date the FMLA leave is to start, and if an employee is on non-FMLA leave when reaching 12-month eligibility, any portion of the leave taken for an FMLA-qualifying reason after meeting eligibility is FMLA leave."
      }
    },
    {
      "unit": "F016",
      "unit_attributes": {
        "kind": "prohibition",
        "scope_quotes": [
          "F016"
        ],
        "scope_text": "Under 29 CFR 825.110(e) regarding worksite employee counts and subsequent workforce changes.",
        "context_quotes": [],
        "modality_quote": "may not",
        "modality": "must_not",
        "alternative_quotes": [],
        "choice_quote": "",
        "choice_text": "",
        "logic_quote": "F016",
        "references": [],
        "statement": "Whether 50 employees are employed within 75 miles to ascertain eligibility is determined when the employee gives notice of the need for leave; once determined eligible for that notice, eligibility is not affected by any subsequent change in employee count, and an employer may not terminate employee leave that has already started if the employee count drops below 50."
      }
    }
  ]
}

unit_attributes.scope_text: For employees of a covered employer under 29 CFR 825.110(a).
unit_attributes.choice_text: An eligible employee must satisfy all three criteria: (1) has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, and (2) has been employed for at least 1,250 hours of service during the 12-month period immediately preceding the commencement of the leave, and (3) is employed at a worksite where 50 or more employees are employed by the employer within 75 miles of that worksite.
unit_attributes.statement: An eligible employee is defined as an employee of a covered employer who has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, has been employed for at least 1,250 hours of service during the 12-month period immediately preceding the commencement of the leave, and is employed at a worksite where 50 or more employees are employed by the employer within 75 miles of that worksite.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining the 12 months an employee must have been employed by the employer under 29 CFR 825.110(b).
unit_attributes.statement: The 12 months an employee must have been employed by the employer need not be consecutive months, provided the rules governing breaks in service are met.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining whether an employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months, subject to the exceptions provided in paragraph (b)(2).
unit_attributes.statement: Subject to the exceptions provided in paragraph (b)(2) of this section, employment periods prior to a break in service of seven years or more need not be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining whether an employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months where there is a break in service of more than seven years under paragraph (b)(2).
unit_attributes.choice_text: Employment periods preceding a break in service of more than seven years must be counted where either: (i) the break in service is occasioned by fulfillment of USERRA-covered service obligation, or (ii) a written agreement, including a collective bargaining agreement, exists concerning the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break in service.
unit_attributes.statement: Employment periods preceding a break in service of more than seven years must be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months where the employee's break in service is occasioned by fulfillment of a USERRA-covered service obligation (and the period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service must also be counted, without providing any greater entitlement than available under USERRA), or where a written agreement, including a collective bargaining agreement, exists concerning the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break in service.

unit_attributes.scope_text: When an employee is maintained on the payroll for any part of a week, or when determining whether intermittent/occasional/casual employment qualifies as at least 12 months.
unit_attributes.statement: If an employee is maintained on the payroll for any part of a week, including any periods of paid or unpaid leave (sick, vacation) during which other benefits or compensation are provided by the employer (such as workers' compensation or group health plan benefits), the week counts as a week of employment; for intermittent, occasional, or casual employment, 52 weeks is deemed equal to 12 months.

unit_attributes.scope_text: When an employer chooses to recognize prior employment before a continuous break in service of more than seven years in determining whether an employee met the 12-month requirement.
unit_attributes.statement: Nothing prevents employers from considering employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years when determining whether an employee has met the 12-month employment requirement, but if an employer chooses to recognize such prior employment, the employer must do so uniformly with respect to all employees with similar breaks in service.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In determining whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service, except as provided in paragraph (c)(2) and § 825.801 for airline flight crew employees.
unit_attributes.statement: Except as provided in paragraph (c)(2) and § 825.801, whether an employee has worked the minimum 1,250 hours of service is determined according to FLSA principles for compensable hours of work based on actual hours worked for the employer, unconstrained by recordkeeping methods or inaccurate compensation agreements, and any accurate accounting of actual hours worked under FLSA principles may be used.

unit_attributes.scope_text: When determining FMLA eligibility for an employee returning from USERRA-covered service.
unit_attributes.statement: An employee returning from USERRA-covered service shall be credited with the hours of service that would have been performed but for the period of absence from work due to or necessitated by USERRA-covered service (added to hours actually worked during the previous 12-month period to meet the hours of service requirement), and the employee's pre-service work schedule can generally be used for calculations.

unit_attributes.scope_text: In the event an employer does not maintain an accurate record of hours worked by an employee, including FLSA recordkeeping-exempt employees.
unit_attributes.statement: In the event an employer does not maintain an accurate record of hours worked by an employee (including FLSA-exempt employees), the employer has the burden of showing that the employee has not worked the requisite hours, and must be able to clearly demonstrate that the employee did not work 1,250 hours during the previous 12 months in order to claim that the employee is not eligible for FMLA leave.

unit_attributes.scope_text: Under 29 CFR 825.110(d) regarding the timing of eligibility determinations.
unit_attributes.statement: The determination of whether an employee meets the hours of service requirement and has been employed by the employer for a total of at least 12 months must be made as of the date the FMLA leave is to start, and if an employee is on non-FMLA leave when reaching 12-month eligibility, any portion of the leave taken for an FMLA-qualifying reason after meeting eligibility is FMLA leave.

unit_attributes.scope_text: Under 29 CFR 825.110(e) regarding worksite employee counts and subsequent workforce changes.
unit_attributes.statement: Whether 50 employees are employed within 75 miles to ascertain eligibility is determined when the employee gives notice of the need for leave; once determined eligible for that notice, eligibility is not affected by any subsequent change in employee count, and an employer may not terminate employee leave that has already started if the employee count drops below 50.
